statements.subject: message
statements.description: A control bit occupying no sequence space, indicating that this segment contains data that must be pushed through to the receiving user.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A control bit (reset), occupying no sequence space, indicating that the receiver should delete the connection without further interaction.
actions: delete the connection without further interaction

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The receiver can determine, based on the sequence number and acknowledgment fields of the incoming segment, whether it should honor the reset command or ignore it.
actions: evaluate SEG.SEQ and SEG.ACK to determine whether to honor or ignore the RST

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An Option field may contain several options, and each option may be several octets in length.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The range of new sequence numbers that may be emitted by a TCP implementation lies between SND.NXT and SND.UNA + SND.WND - 1.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A control bit (urgent), occupying no sequence space, used to indicate that the receiving user should be notified to do urgent processing as long as there is data to be consumed with sequence numbers less than the value indicated by the urgent pointer.
